solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Siren primarily voluptuous menace to sailors

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a voluptuous figure is a curvy one

explanation.surface: A shapely siren luring sailors to their doom, like the ones Odysseus sailed past.
explanation.walkthrough: The sirens of myth were the danger to sailors, so 'Siren' looks like the definition; here it only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurvy, caused by lack of vitamin C, was the classic disease killing crews on long voyages.

clue.text: Grass to rub off Alsatian's seat

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are not in their proper arrangement

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting grass stains off the seat of a dog, an Alsatian being a German shepherd.
explanation.walkthrough: An Alsatian is the British name for a German shepherd dog, which steers you to a dog's bottom; here Alsatian means a person from Alsace.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of the Alsace region of France, so it is the regional seat for anyone from there.

clue.text: Open new account upset charges increase

indicators.note: to charge something is to load or fill it, so one piece is packed inside another

parts.note: to up something is to increase it
N is the standard abbreviation for new

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A bank customer opens a new account, only to be upset that the charges have gone up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'charges increase' as a noun and verb; in fact 'charges' is the containment instruction and 'increase' is the verb UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap a bottle or pen is to take its lid off, which is to open it.

clue.text: Drive taking M4 the other way

indicators.note: going the other way means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A motorist's route choice: heading down the M4 motorway, westbound out of London rather than towards it.
explanation.walkthrough: The M4 is a British motorway from London to Wales; read cryptically, its 4 is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Vim is energy and vigour, the same sense as drive meaning ambition and get-up-and-go.

clue.text: Celebrated victory, sounding that confident

indicators.note: sounding that means said in a way that resembles it, so the spoken form is what counts

parts.note: celebrated in song is sang; a victory is a win

explanation.surface: Fans singing after a victory, sounding sure their team will keep winning.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, the past tense of sing followed by a win runs together as the four-syllable adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanguine person is optimistic and cheerfully hopeful, which is close to being self-assured about outcomes.

clue.text: Very common adjective journalist's writing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a word like 'the' or 'a', which old grammars class as adjectives and which are the commonest words in English
second meaning: a piece written for a newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: Traditional grammar treats 'a' and 'the' as a kind of adjective, and 'the' is the single most frequent English word, hence very common.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical term covers the determiners 'a', 'an' and 'the'; the press term covers any written news piece.

clue.text: Eery quality publican notes in empty gents

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is enclosed by it
an empty word has had its insides cleared out, leaving just its two outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a publican is the host who runs a pub
short written notes are lines, as in dropping someone a line

explanation.surface: A pub landlord leaving notes in a deserted gents' toilet, which has an unsettling feel.
explanation.walkthrough: The gents is the British name for a men's public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Eery is a variant spelling of eerie, and the noun names the spooky, spectral character of something haunted.

clue.text: Next time swimming across different channels

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it on both sides, enclosing it
swimming letters are swirling about, so they settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
media are channels of communication, plural like channels

explanation.surface: A swimming event scheduled for next time, broadcast across several TV channels.
explanation.walkthrough: The four shuffled letters split two and two around the five-letter piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Next in a sequence is immediate, coming directly after with nothing in between.

clue.text: German's sterling kept by Czech tourist

indicators.note: something kept by another is held within it, so the letters sit inside these words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A Czech tourist holding on to some British pounds sterling that a German handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterling here is not money but the adjective meaning genuine; the German word for genuine has passed into English.
explanation.definitionFit: The German adjective means authentic or real, and sterling as an adjective means of solid, genuine worth.

clue.text: Old Cambridge professor went dancing and running

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move around into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: An elderly don who once went dancing and running, lively for his age.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'went' as a verb with the dancing and running; it is only letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton held the Lucasian chair of mathematics at Cambridge in the seventeenth century, long ago.

clue.text: Lying copper married criminal after romance on vacation

indicators.note: after places one part behind another in the reading order
a place on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
M is the abbreviation for married
bent is slang for corrupt or criminal

explanation.surface: A dishonest policeman who married a crook after a holiday romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' seems to describe a dishonest copper, but it is the definition in its other sense; copper is the metal, not the police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent describes someone lying down or reclining, the posture rather than the dishonesty.

clue.text: Energy zero, speed corresponding to that?

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
a speed of zero is 0 miles per hour, written 0 mph

explanation.surface: A physics question: if energy is zero, what speed goes with that?
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece refers back to the first: the speed matching zero is 0 mph, so the zero appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour, punch and get-up-and-go, the lively sense of energy.

clue.text: Clever chap sets idiot anagrams

indicators.note: used as a verb, to anagram letters is to rearrange them into a new word

parts.note: the thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A smart fellow who compiles puzzles, setting anagrams for a fool to solve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever chap' looks like one unit, but only the first word is the definition; 'chap' belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophisticated device or argument is complex and ingenious, a common sense of clever.

clue.text: Private jet back in first world on shorter round trip

parts.note: inner thoughts are private ones
a jet is a kind of aircraft

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Travelling by private jet in first class on a quick round trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First world' looks like a phrase, but 'first' only supplies its last letter and 'world' starts the definition; 'round trip' is an orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars orbit nearer the Sun than the outer ones, so their circuits around it are shorter.

clue.text: According to Spooner, courts at night become lighter

indicators.note: Spooner was known for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds trade places

parts.note: to court is to woo; with the L sound from the next word up front, it is said 'looz'
at night is late; taking the W sound in place of its L, it is said 'wait'

explanation.surface: A courtroom image: judges sitting into the night until the place becomes lighter at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' suggests daybreak after a night session, but it is about body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sheds pounds on a diet ends up lighter on the scales, the bodily sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Regulation in force around Brittany town, but fine cancelled

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it
something cancelled is struck out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Dinan is a walled medieval town in Brittany

explanation.surface: A local rule in force around a Breton town, though the fine for breaking it has been waived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In force' reads as a phrase, but 'in' just links the definition and the force is a word to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official decree or local by-law, a kind of regulation issued by an authority.

clue.text: Really upset Hindu god, say

parts.note: a deva is a divine being in Hinduism
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a Hindu deity has been genuinely angered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is the verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To devastate someone is to shatter them emotionally, leaving them very distressed.

clue.text: Turned back some who had illegal ID

indicators.note: turned back means facing the opposite way, so the letters run right to left
some means a portion, so only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters straddle the three words

explanation.surface: Border staff turning away people carrying fake identity documents.
explanation.walkthrough: ID looks like identity card, but it is the postal abbreviation for a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: ID is the official two-letter US postal code for the northwestern state.

clue.text: Typical dog runs too much

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
over as a prefix means excessive, as in overdo

explanation.surface: A dog that, like all dogs, runs about far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'runs' a verb about the dog; it is just an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rover is the stereotypical name for a pet hound, the generic name everyone gives a pooch.

clue.text: Soldier on a grave

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'a' in 'once a week'
a grave situation is a severe one

explanation.surface: A soldier lying on a grave, a war memorial picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' looks like a soldier standing on a tomb; it is the phrasal verb. 'A' as in 'ten pounds a head' means per.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to keep going despite difficulty, which is exactly to keep trying steadfastly.

clue.text: Gap to be fixed, soaking fuel store?

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or rigged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A leaking gap that needs mending, letting water soak into a storeroom of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Gap' and 'to be' supply letters, so 'to be' is both letters and the join; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog is waterlogged ground and the peat cut from it is burned as fuel, so it is a wet store of fuel.

clue.text: Gunners count with large intervals

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
to count on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Artillerymen counting off with big gaps between the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunners' is also the nickname of Arsenal football club, but here it is the army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens rarely occurs seldom, separated by long gaps of time.

clue.text: Writer's original surname is Dahl

indicators.note: something original is novel and inventive, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: the thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A trivia claim that some author's real family name is Dahl, like the children's writer Roald Dahl.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; the real writer named Dahl is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The British-Indian novelist wrote Midnight's Children and The Satanic Verses, a famous literary figure.

clue.text: Refuse piece of cake that Republican cuts

indicators.note: a knife that cuts goes into what it slices, so these letters end up lodged inside

parts.note: a doss is British slang for an easy task
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A politician turning down a slice of cake that a Republican is cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb decline, but the definition is the noun meaning rubbish; 'piece of cake' means something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste, originally the scum skimmed from molten metal, so it is rubbish.

clue.text: Supplier of hydro power affected by water?

parts.note: a dam drives a hydroelectric plant
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A hydroelectric generator whose output depends on the flow of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hydro power' reads as one phrase; the split falls between them, with 'power' supplying a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damp is slightly wet, moistened by water, as the question mark playfully hints.

clue.text: Military leader elected for another term?

parts.note: an aga was a commander in the Ottoman Empire
a candidate who is elected gets in

explanation.surface: A general voted back into office for a second term in power.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the stretch: the word is literally another term for 'once more', as well as a second term of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, a repeat occurrence, just as a second term repeats a period in office.

clue.text: No object you throw comes back in vast Aussie backwater

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: vast means very big

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it went, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a ball is something thrown

explanation.surface: An object you throw that comes back in the vast Australian outback: a boomerang, by implication.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers you to a boomerang, which returns when thrown; but 'No object you throw' is a cricket term, an illegal delivery bowled by the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is an Australian oxbow lake or stagnant pool left by a river, a backwater in the literal sense.

clue.text: Walls with bearings removed on each side

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so those letters are struck out of the word at its edges

parts.note: taken as written
compass bearings: W for west and S for south
surface padding: it completes the phrase saying the cut happens at both ends of the word

explanation.surface: Walls with the support bearings knocked out of both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters lost happen to be compass points at either end, which is why the clue calls them bearings and says 'on each side'; 'each' also serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: All and each both cover every member of a group, the whole lot taken together or one by one.

clue.text: Honour litter bearer carrying others back from battle

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a sow bears a litter of piglets
the others are the rest

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A stretcher-bearer winning honour by carrying wounded comrades back from the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: A litter is also a stretcher, which is the picture the surface paints; here it is a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is high standing and esteem earned through achievement, close to honour as public regard.

clue.text: Finish last in cricket in which you're not out?

parts.note: to finish is to close

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bats last and is left not out at the end of the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out' is a cricket term for a batter still in at the end, but here it means not having come out about one's sexuality.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has not openly declared being gay is said to be in the closet, hiding it.
